_note: Evergreen editorial seed pool for troubadour-quarterly, written by Claude on 2026-11-05 for owner review. Tips, ideas, real tools (homepage links only) and generic opportunities. No news: news only comes from the brand's listed feeds. Edit freely.

items.title: Keep a quarterly review of what you built and what you learned
items.summary: Four pages: wins, mistakes, lessons and the next bet.

items.title: Design one system that runs without you
items.summary: Write it down so someone else could run it.

items.title: Look at one artwork for ten full minutes
items.summary: Past the first reaction, a picture keeps giving.

items.title: Visit a gallery on its quiet day
items.summary: You can stand where you like and look as long as you like.

items.title: Sketch what you cannot photograph
items.summary: Drawing makes you look properly.

items.title: Start a small collection of postcards or prints
items.summary: Cheap, personal and a good reason to visit museum shops.

items.title: Trade a drawing a week with a friend
items.summary: A low-pressure habit that adds up.

items.title: Map the murals and sculptures in your town
items.summary: Turn your walk home into a small public art tour.

items.title: Google Arts & Culture
items.summary: Explore artworks and exhibitions from museums around the world.

items.title: Europeana
items.summary: Millions of digitized artworks, books and recordings from European institutions.

items.title: The Met Collection
items.summary: Browse and download open-access images from The Metropolitan Museum of Art.

items.title: Volunteer at a gallery or arts festival
items.summary: Volunteers see behind the scenes and often get free entry.

items.title: Join a life-drawing session
items.summary: Many studios run affordable open sessions.

items.title: Read the footnotes of any financial claim
items.summary: The caveats that matter are rarely in the headline.

items.title: Track what you own and owe once a month
items.summary: A simple list beats a vague feeling about money.

items.title: Follow one commodity for a month
items.summary: Salt, wheat or copper. Note what moves it and what does not.

items.title: Build a one-page model of a small business you admire
items.summary: Where does the money come in and where does it go?

items.title: FRED
items.summary: Free economic data from the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis.

items.title: World Bank Open Data
items.summary: Free global development data by country and topic.

items.title: Take a free personal-finance course
items.summary: Libraries and universities publish good ones.
